articles.summary_en: A new study links walking about 3,000 steps a day to slower Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, less harmful tau buildup and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline; benefits appeared strongest at 5,000 steps.

articles.title_en: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
articles.summary_en: Scientists have won the 2026 Nobel Prize for optogenetics, a technique that uses light to switch brain cells on and off; it has helped activate memories and may aid vision restoration and brain disorder treatments.

articles.title: 物理学家创造出名为“分数量子费米海”的新奇量子态
articles.summary: 物理学家在超冷原子中发现一种新量子物态，原子形成高度激发却有序的“分数量子费米海”；该结果挑战既有量子理论，并暗示可能存在奇异准粒子。
articles.title_en: Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea
articles.summary_en: Physicists have created a new quantum state, the fractional Fermi sea, in ultracold atoms; the highly excited but orderly configuration challenges established quantum theory and hints at exotic quasiparticles.
articles.original_title: Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea
articles.reason: 报道超冷原子中分数量子费米海的实验发现及其对量子理论的挑战。
articles.reason_en: Reports an experimental discovery of the fractional Fermi sea in ultracold atoms and its challenge to quantum theory.

subsections.briefing_title: 科学研究：磁性新形态、阿尔茨海默病步行关联与光遗传学诺奖
subsections.briefing_summary: 四项研究进展显示：交错磁性发现获重要物理学奖，挑战百余年物理认知；每日约3000步与阿尔茨海默病相关脑变化较慢、tau蛋白积累较少及认知和功能衰退减半相关，益处似乎在5000步时最强；光遗传学获2026年诺贝尔奖，为记忆激活、视力恢复和脑病治疗带来可能；超冷原子中实现高度激发却有序的“分数量子费米海”，挑战既有量子理论并暗示奇异准粒子。
subsections.briefing_title_en: Science research: a new magnetism form, Alzheimer's walking link and optogenetics Nobel
subsections.briefing_summary_en: Four research developments: the discovery of altermagnetism won a major physics prize, challenging longstanding physics; about 3,000 daily steps were linked to slower Alzheimer's-related brain changes, less harmful tau buildup and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, with benefits appearing strongest at 5,000 steps; optogenetics won the 2026 Nobel Prize, offering possibilities for activating memories, restoring vision and treating brain disorders; and a highly excited but orderly fractional Fermi sea was created in ultracold atoms, challenging established quantum theory and hinting at exotic quasiparticles.
